title: Backward compat — `python -m jarvis_orchestrate <plan>` continues to work after pipx install
body: Phase A introduces the `jarvis` console script as the canonical invocation, but the existing `python -m jarvis_orchestrate <plan>` invocation MUST keep working. Reason: (a) the maintainer's own dogfood plans + scripts assume the module-invoke form; flag-day-breaking them slows down dogfood iteration; (b) F022 OSS-readiness work documented `python -m` extensively in README sections that downstream agents may have memorized — breaking those mid-pipeline-migration creates churn for no reason; (c) supporting both is essentially free (Python's package layout already supports both entry points). How to apply: any later phase that adds a NEW invocation surface should similarly avoid breaking `python -m` for at least one full plan cycle. Document the migration path in a future phase if `python -m` becomes burden; do not break it speculatively now.

title: pipx, not pip, is the canonical install path
body: Jarvis is a global tool, not a project dependency. pipx isolates Jarvis's own dependencies (pydantic, firebase-admin, etc.) from any project venv the user is working in. `pip install jarvis-orchestrate` (per-project) would clash with project deps, force version juggling, and confuse the global-tool model the rest of Phase A is built around. Reason: (a) every other modern Python global tool (poetry, ruff, pre-commit, datasette) ships pipx-first for the same reason; (b) the friend / OSS-user audience targeted by Phase A is exactly the audience that hits dependency conflicts when global tools are pip-installed; (c) pipx makes upgrades atomic — `pipx upgrade jarvis-orchestrate` doesn't disturb any project. How to apply: README quickstart leads with pipx; `pip install -e .` is documented only as a developer-mode alternative for Jarvis contributors. The console-script entry point is configured the same way for both, so the technical surface is identical — the difference is install hygiene.

title: Project registry name regex `^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9-]{0,63}$` — lowercase, hyphen-separated, no underscores, max 64 chars
body: Project names in the registry follow the same shape as DNS labels and most package-name conventions: lowercase, hyphen-separated, no underscores, no uppercase, no special chars, no leading hyphen, ≤64 chars. Reason: (a) names appear in CLI args (`jarvis projects show foo`), filesystem paths (`<project>/.jarvis/`), JSON keys, and likely future URL paths in Phase D's MCP tool args; permissive names create ambiguity in any of those contexts; (b) DNS-label conventions are universally understood, low-cognitive-load, and avoid the `_` vs `-` shell-quoting hazards; (c) 64 chars is plenty for human-meaningful names but short enough to fit in tabular output. Cross-field invariant: the registered path must exist as a directory at add time. How to apply: any future Phase A/B/C/D registry-adjacent identifier (intake-brief IDs, agent IDs, MCP tool names) should follow the same regex unless there's a specific reason to diverge.

title: Override precedence at dispatch — per-project `.jarvis/jarvis.json` > global `~/.jarvis/config.json` > hardcoded fallbacks
body: When the supervisor needs an implementer / auditor / tier / target_env / plans_dir / human_gates / protected_paths value at dispatch time, it consults sources in this order: (1) per-project `<project>/.jarvis/jarvis.json` (committable, project-specific); (2) global `~/.jarvis/config.json` (per-user defaults); (3) hardcoded fallbacks (e.g., implementer='claude', auditor='codex'). The first non-None match wins per field. Reason: (a) different projects use different stacks (Swift on SpinDine vs Python on Jarvis itself vs TypeScript on Glam) — agent pair must be configurable per-project; (b) committing the per-project config means the project's expected agent setup travels with the repo, so a friend cloning the repo gets the right defaults without copying the operator's home dir; (c) global config exists so a user with several similar projects doesn't have to repeat themselves. How to apply: any new config field that varies by project should land in per-project config first; only promote to global when the field genuinely is per-user (e.g., calibration paths). Don't add fields to both layers unless there's a clear semantic reason.

title: Phase A locks alone — Phases B/C/D are NOT bundled
body: Phase A is locked as its own plan. Phases B (project init + discovery), C (intake pipeline), and D (agent discovery + MCP) are outlined in `docs/ROADMAP.md` but explicitly NOT locked yet. Reason: (a) the install + registry surface will surface real friction (pipx version conflicts, pyproject.toml structure choices, Python version constraints, registry-path conventions, etc.) that we cannot fully predict from inside the source tree; (b) those discoveries shape Phase B's `jarvis init` design and Phase D's MCP tool surface — locking B/C/D speculatively now would commit to interfaces before we know what real-world Phase A use teaches us; (c) this is the same demand-driven discipline the substrate followed (D012 of plan 003: defer next-version plans on a real-world signal, not calendar). How to apply: when Phase A ships, only THEN draft Phase B as its own plan with locked decisions. Don't pre-decide Phase B's interfaces from inside Phase A's lock cycle.

title: Per-project `.jarvis/jarvis.json` is committable; global `~/.jarvis/config.json` is NOT
body: The per-project config file lives at `<project>/.jarvis/jarvis.json` (under the project's git tree) and is intended to be committed. The global config at `~/.jarvis/config.json` is per-user and is NOT under git control. Reason: (a) per-project config encodes the project's expected agent pair, plans dir, gates, protected paths — these travel with the repo so any contributor (or friend cloning) gets correct defaults without copying the operator's setup; (b) global config holds per-user preferences (calibration paths, default tier preference, pointers to local quota state) — committing those would leak operator identity / cross-project tuning into every repo; (c) the `.jarvis/` directory inside a project becomes a stable namespace for future per-project artifacts (intake briefs, project-scoped INBOX, project-scoped audit log) that are also commit-worthy. How to apply: any new Phase B/C/D file that's project-specific lands under `<project>/.jarvis/`; user-specific files land under `~/.jarvis/`. Cross-file leakage (e.g., embedding home-dir paths into committed configs) is a smell.

title: F001 scope cut — packaging + --version + global config helpers ONLY; registry/per-project wiring deferred to F002/F003
body: F001 as it shipped is narrower than the original features.json acceptance list. What landed: (1) PEP 621 pyproject.toml with [project.scripts] jarvis console-script entry point and [tool.setuptools.dynamic] version reading from `jarvis_orchestrate.__version__` (single source of truth); (2) `jarvis --version` / `-V` flag handled at the top of cli.main; (3) backward-compat path `python -m jarvis_orchestrate --version` verified by a subprocess test; (4) global_config module (GlobalConfig Pydantic model, jarvis_home() with $JARVIS_HOME override for test isolation, load_config/save_config/merge_with_defaults helpers); (5) 27 tests across 7 classes proving no repo-specific assumptions (works from arbitrary cwd, $JARVIS_HOME points anywhere). Cut from F001: original step 4 (wiring global config into supervisor's _approve_main / _resume_main / dispatch-from-plan / dispatch_volley lookups) and step 5 (README rewrite to lead with `pipx install jarvis-orchestrate`). Reason for cutting: (a) supervisor wiring is most natural in F003 alongside per-project override precedence (D004) — wiring it in F001 would mean re-touching the same code paths twice; (b) README pipx-quickstart edits depend on F002's project-add UX existing first (otherwise quickstart can't show the canonical workflow end-to-end); (c) acceptance items #2/#3 (`pipx install .` and `pip install -e .` smoke tests) are operator-side manual verifications outside the test surface — they stay as F002/F003 close-out gates, not F001's. How to apply: when closing F002, verify (a) `pipx install .` from a fresh shell + `which jarvis` → pipx-managed binary; (b) README quickstart updated to lead with pipx; (c) PYTHONPATH=scripts removed from primary instructions. When closing F003, wire global config into the supervisor lookups + verify override precedence per D004. F001 close-out artifacts: pyproject.toml, scripts/jarvis_orchestrate/__init__.py (version), scripts/jarvis_orchestrate/global_config.py (new), scripts/jarvis_orchestrate/cli.py (--version handling), scripts/jarvis_orchestrate/tests/test_f001_packaging_and_global_config.py (new, 27 tests). Verification: 27/27 targeted, 607+6 skipped full suite, ruff clean, sanitization 0 findings.

title: F002 surface decisions — --force requires --yes (no TTY prompts), --json across all subcommands, whole-second timestamps, single env-var spec
body:
F002 ships project-registry CRUD as a self-contained module + CLI subcommands. Several surface decisions worth recording so F003 / future surfaces stay consistent:

(1) **--force requires --yes for non-interactive use.** The original spec mentioned `add --force` could prompt interactively OR skip the prompt with `--yes`. We refused the interactive-prompt path entirely: in a CLI orchestration system, every invocation may be agent-driven, and adding a TTY-prompting dependency creates ambiguity (does the agent see the prompt? does it deadlock waiting for stdin?). Surface is now: bare `add foo /p` refuses on collision with exit 2; `add foo /p --force` without `--yes` refuses with exit 2 + a one-line message naming `--yes`; `add foo /p --force --yes` overwrites silently. Reason: keeps the surface deterministic for cron / Discord / agent dispatch without losing the intent of the safety rail. How to apply: any future destructive flag in F003 / Phase B/C/D follows the same pattern — destructive intent is two-flag (intent + confirm), not one-flag-with-prompt.

(2) **--json on every subcommand.** All four subcommands (add/list/show/remove) accept --json. The dry-run preview from `remove` also has a --json shape so an automated pipeline can detect dry-run-vs-deleted without screen-scraping. Reason: agents shelling out are first-class consumers of this CLI (per Phase D's MCP intent); requiring them to parse human-readable output would be brittle. How to apply: every Phase B/C/D CLI subcommand that returns structured data must offer a `--json` shape from day one.

(3) **Whole-second ISO-8601 UTC timestamps.** `created_at` and `last_used_at` are stamped at second precision (`%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ`), not microsecond. Reason: operators inspect `~/.jarvis/projects.json` directly; sub-second precision creates churn in `git diff`-style review without adding signal. The `update_last_used` test pins idempotency-within-same-second as a deliberate property: stamping twice in the same second is OK and produces equal output. How to apply: any future per-user JSON file (intake briefs, project-scoped INBOX timestamps) follows whole-second precision unless there's a strict ordering need.

(4) **Single env-var spec for registry-path override.** The original features.json mentioned a separate `$JARVIS_REGISTRY_PATH` env var. We did not add one — the registry is at `$JARVIS_HOME/projects.json` and `$JARVIS_HOME` already carries the override. Reason: two env vars to remember (`$JARVIS_HOME` for global-config tests, `$JARVIS_REGISTRY_PATH` for registry tests) is a footgun; tests are simpler with one. How to apply: every per-user file under `~/.jarvis/` resolves through `gc.jarvis_home()`. The only reason to add a separate env var is if a specific file needs an independent location for a real user-facing reason — not for test isolation.

F002 close-out artifacts: `scripts/jarvis_orchestrate/projects_registry.py` (new module), `scripts/jarvis_orchestrate/cli.py` (4 subcommand handlers + dispatch), `scripts/jarvis_orchestrate/tests/test_f002_projects_registry.py` (new, 52 tests). Verification: 52/52 targeted, 659+6 skipped full suite, ruff clean, sanitization 0 findings. NO supervisor dispatch behavior changed — the registry is consulted by F003 once the override-precedence chain lands.

title: F003 close-out — accepting volley work despite stopped_no_progress terminal; recording gate-semantics + 600s-timeout caveats
body:
F003 dispatched via volley (claude implementer, codex auditor, max_iter=2) and terminated `stopped_no_progress` after 2 rounds. Both implementer iterations hit the supervisor's hardcoded 600s subprocess timeout — claude completed the F003 implementation work on disk before the wrapper killed it, but the audit envelope JSON didn't flush so each iteration's envelope recorded `audit_status: blocked` / `summary: DISPATCH FAILED: TimeoutExpired`. The codex auditor correctly flagged the broken envelopes as not being valid completion artifacts; the no-progress breaker tripped because the auditor verdict pattern was identical across rounds.

**Why we accept the work despite the non-success terminal**: (a) the 43-test F003 suite is fully green (suite total 702 passed, 6 skipped vs 659 + 6 baseline = +43 with no regressions); (b) ruff is clean across all F003-touched files; (c) sanitization is clean (591 files, 0 findings); (d) the acceptance contract is independently verifiable from on-disk state, not dependent on the audit envelope; (e) operator-side diff review for the 6 high-risk audit-focus areas (missed call sites, precedence, cwd fallback, name/path confusion, None-vs-missing, doctor exits) all check out. Re-dispatching to chase a clean signoff envelope would burn quota cycles without changing the on-disk state.

**Caveat 1 — gate semantics**: Plan declares `human_gates: [pre_impl, pre_merge]`, but the supervisor evaluates declared gates as a single upfront admission set (per the 2026-04-29 dogfood lesson, recorded in feedback memory). Operator cleared BOTH gates upfront so iteration 0 could run. Operator-side review post-volley substituted for the platform-enforced merge gate this round. **Lifecycle-staged gates remain a queued platform improvement, not part of F003.**

**Caveat 2 — 600s subprocess timeout**: The supervisor's hardcoded subprocess deadline is too short for cross-cutting features that add ~1000+ lines across multiple modules + tests. Both implementer iterations completed real work but were killed before flushing audit envelopes. **A separate platform slice should raise the cap (perhaps to 1800s) and/or refactor audit_writer to checkpoint-as-you-go so a timeout produces a partial-but-readable envelope instead of a fully-blocked terminal.**

**Caveat 3 — `_resolve_plan_dir` Step-4 cwd fallback**: claude implemented a deliberate `<cwd>/docs/plans/<plan-id>` carveout for un-registered repos. It's gated by file existence + only fires after registry-based resolution fails. Documented in the function docstring. Bounded risk — cannot silently pick up a stray plan from another registered project (those are caught by Step 2/3). Acceptable as ergonomic carveout for the bare `jarvis` smoke-test from un-registered repos.

**Caveat 4 — approve/resume not wired through resolver**: claude judged that `cli._approve_main` / `cli._resume_main` clear gates, they don't pick agents, so they don't need the precedence resolver. Rationale documented in `test_f003_project_config.py` docstring (Audit-focus addendum item 7). If a future feature adds agent-aware behavior to approve/resume, the resolver should be wired in then.

**Spec-clarification finding dismissed**: The codex auditor's i1 finding asking for WARN to NOT exit non-zero contradicts the locked F003 acceptance ('exit code: 0 if all PASS, 1 if any WARN, 2 if any FAIL'). Per scope discipline we honor the spec literally; if the spec is wrong, that's a separate ticket.

F003 close-out artifacts: scripts/jarvis_orchestrate/project_config.py (new), scripts/jarvis_orchestrate/cli.py (modified), scripts/jarvis_orchestrate/supervisor.py (modified), scripts/jarvis_doctor.py (modified), scripts/jarvis_orchestrate/plan_loader.py (modified), scripts/jarvis_orchestrate/tests/test_f003_project_config.py (new — 43 tests). Volley audit envelopes preserved at docs/plans/2026-05-03-001-feat-global-install-project-registry/audit/{claude-implementer-F003-i0.json, claude-implementer-F003-i1.json, codex-auditor-F003-i0.json, codex-auditor-F003-i1.json, transcript.md, gate-state.json, signoff-2026-05-03-001-feat-global-install-project-registry.json}.

title: Plan close-out — status flip active → completed via exempt-flow
body:
Third close-out in the Tier 1 close-out batch (after Plan 2026-05-04-001 canonical-module flip and Plan 2026-05-02-003 nested-orch v1). All three features (F001 + F002 + F003) shipped passes:true. F001/F002 via direct path; F003 via volley with terminal `stopped_no_progress` operator-accepted on direct review per D009 (work landed clean on disk; only audit envelopes blocked from flushing due to 600s subprocess deadline).

Close-out discipline executed: (1) `git ls-tree HEAD -- docs/plans/2026-05-03-001-feat-global-install-project-registry/` enumerated 14 tracked files; worktree `find` matched exactly — no partial-clone fallout (unlike Plan 2026-05-02-003 where decisions.jsonl was tracked-but-absent). (2) Validate exits 0 across plan.md frontmatter, features.json, and all 5 schema-validated audit envelopes (4 implementer/auditor i0+i1, 1 signoff); auxiliary `audit/gate-state.json` skipped per validator policy. (3) Per-feature evidence already comprehensive (`evidence/f001-closeout-memo.md`, `f002-closeout-memo.md`, `f003-closeout-memo.md`); D-history captures lock + scope + close-out reasoning (D001–D009 including D009's full F003 acceptance reasoning). (4) Plan-level memo written at `evidence/plan-closeout-memo.md` — adds value beyond per-feature evidence by: (i) cross-feature synthesis F001+F002+F003, (ii) cross-link to follow-up plans `2026-05-04-002-fix-supervisor-lifecycle-staged-gates` (lifecycle gates) + `2026-05-04-003-fix-subprocess-timeout-envelope-durability` (timeout cap + envelope durability) that consumed F003's caveats #1 and #2 as their own scope, (iii) brand-rename note (this plan was authored pre-`8edd953` so plan text references `~/.jarvis/` + `jarvis projects` — current canonical surfaces are `~/.dontpanic/` + `dontpanic projects`, with legacy paths still readable via shim), (iv) Phase A → B/C/D arc framing (Phases B/C/D demand-driven, not drafted). It explicitly does NOT re-cover F003's diff review or D009's acceptance reasoning. (5) D010 appended without reconstructing existing entries — single-line append after verifying D001–D009 sequence is intact. (6) `dontpanic plan close docs/plans/2026-05-03-001-feat-global-install-project-registry/` — `goal_type=None` (no goal-governance classification declared) consumes the exempt-by-absence branch of the F2 completion gate. (7) Re-validate exits 0 with `status: completed`. (8) Commit scoped to this plan dir only.

Reason: this plan is the access-layer foundation for the broader service-mode arc. F001/F002/F003 deliver pipx-installable global binary + project-registry CRUD + per-project config with override precedence + doctor preflight integration. F003's audit envelopes captured a real-world signal of two platform weaknesses (gate semantics + subprocess timeout) which became their own follow-up plans rather than F003 expansions, preserving Phase A's scope discipline. Closing eliminates the 'shipped-but-active' awkwardness in the memory index and enables the post-rename canonical-CLI experience to anchor on a closed-parent substrate.

How to apply: nested orchestration is NOT used for this close-out (operator-confirmed this turn) — close-out is mechanical paperwork, not auditor-finding-driven dispatch work. Phase B/C/D drafting remains demand-driven (per the substrate-vs-layer discipline established at Plan 2026-05-02-003 D012); the trigger for each is a real workflow that exposes the gap, not a calendar.
